question.problem: What is the parametrization of the curve $r(t)=⟨{t}^{4},\,\frac{1}{2}{t}^{4}+2,\,3-{t}^{4}⟩,$ $t\ge 0,$ by its arc length $s?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{2}{t}^{4}+2),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3-{t}^{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨4{t}^{3},\,2{t}^{3},\,-4{t}^{3}⟩ \\  & =2{t}^{3}⟨2,\,1,\,-2⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =|2{t}^{3}|\sqrt{{(2)}^{2}+{(1)}^{2}+(-2)^{2}} \\  & =2{t}^{3}\sqrt{4+1+4} \\  & =6{t}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the arc length of the curve from $0$ to $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}s & ={\int }_{0}^{t}‖{r}^{′}(u)‖\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{t}6{u}^{3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =6{\int }_{0}^{t}{u}^{3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{u}^{4}\,{|}_{0}^{t} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{t}^{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $s=\frac{3}{2}{t}^{4}$ and $t\ge 0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2}{t}^{4} & =s \\ {t}^{4} & =\frac{2s}{3} \\ t & =\sqrt[4]{\frac{2s}{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector function that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\sqrt[4]{\frac{2s}{3}}) \\  & =⟨{(\sqrt[4]{\frac{2s}{3}})}^{4},\,\frac{1}{2}{(\sqrt[4]{\frac{2s}{3}})}^{4}+2,\,3-{(\sqrt[4]{\frac{2s}{3}})}^{4}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2s}{3},\,\frac{s}{3}+2,\,3-\frac{2s}{3}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨2s,\,s+6,\,9-2s⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
